- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon (especially first 5–10 days), then underestimates later — suggest adjusting for mean reversion toward historical median.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — apply dampening factor or lagged momentum correction.
- Forecast often lags true price movements by 1–3 days — consider adding 1-day lagged true value as a smoothing anchor.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in mid-to-late forecast — may reflect overconfidence in downward trends; consider adding upward volatility buffer.
- When true price drops sharply (e.g., 85→80), model often fails to recognize the drop — apply “drop-trigger” rule: if true price falls >5% from prior day, reduce forecast by 2–3%.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high prices — if last 5 days are above 88, model tends to overpredict — apply “recent high cap” rule: cap forecast at 88.5 if recent 5-day avg >88.0.
